dash.balanceHistoryNote: The balance the broker reports, deposits and withdrawals included — unlike the equity curve, which is built from trades and leaves them out on purpose. The difference between the two is exactly the money that was added rather than earned. One point per day the account was synced.

analytics.costsNoShare: The book did not gross a profit, so there is nothing for the costs to be a share of. The absolute figure is the one that means something.
analytics.costsTurnedNote: Right about the trade, still down on it
analytics.costsBySymbol: By instrument — share of its own gross that costs ate
analytics.riskSpreadHint: Standard deviation of risk over its mean. Under 0.25 is disciplined sizing; over 1.0 means position size is effectively random — and then the win rate says nothing, because the wins and the losses are not the same size.
analytics.topShareHint: Share of gross profit from the {count} biggest winners. High is not automatically bad — a trend follower is supposed to look like this — but it changes what every other number means.
analytics.restsOnOneTrade: Without the best trade the book loses
analytics.restsOnOne: Without the best trade — a loss
analytics.underwaterHint: Longest stretch spent below a previous equity peak. Drawdown says how far down; this says how long you stayed there — and that is what makes people abandon a working system.
analytics.byDayLoad: Average day, by how many trades were taken that day
analytics.byPeriodNote: Each month is measured against the balance it opened with, so the percentages compare across years. The same 2,000 is 10% on a 20,000 account and 2.5% on an 80,000 one. A blank month is one with no trading.
analytics.byPeriodNoBase: This account has no deposit in its history, so there is no opening balance to measure against — the table shows money only. Percentages appear once a sync brings the balance movements over from the broker. A blank month is one with no trading.
analytics.heatHint: How much of the defined risk was actually used up, on average, by the trades that ended in profit. Losers are excluded — they reached their stop by definition, so including them measures the stop rather than the heat the trades took. Very low means the stop is wider than the trade needs; near 100% means the winners barely survived.
analytics.throughStop: {count, plural, =0 {no winner went through its stop} one {# winner went past its stop distance and came back} other {# winners went past their stop distance and came back}}
analytics.captureHint: What fraction of the best move a trade ever saw was actually taken. 100% means exiting at the high every time, which nobody does; a book at 30% has an exit problem rather than an entry one.
analytics.bestNote: Closed trades only · minimum 5 trades per category
analytics.holdRatioShort: Winners held for less — the mark of cutting them short
analytics.holdRatioLong: Winners held for longer — the ratio you want
analytics.holdNoPair: Needs both a winning and a losing trade in range

welcome.title: Let's connect your MT5 account
welcome.subtitle: Complete 4 simple steps to get started
welcome.hint: This should take about two minutes

login.title: Step 1: Account number
login.label: MT5 account number
login.hint: Your account number with your broker (like 50214437)
login.help: Where to find it? Open MT5, look at the window title or terminal. Your account number is displayed right there.

server.title: Step 2: Your broker’s server name
server.label: Server name
server.hint: Copy it exactly as MetaTrader shows it — hyphens and digits included.
server.help: Where do I find this? On the phone: Settings → the line under the account name, after the account number (for example "541171171 - FTMO-Server4"). On the desktop: the MetaTrader window title, or File → Login to Trade Account.

password.title: Step 3: Investor password
password.label: Investor password
password.hint: This password allows read-only access (no ability to trade)
password.help: Where to find it? In MT5 Terminal → Tools → Options → Account tab → Investment Password. If you haven't created one yet, you can create it now.

processing.syncing: This may take a few seconds as we connect to the MT5 server

success.title: Done! Your account is connected
success.subtitle: Your data is syncing now
success.status: In a moment you'll see all your data on the dashboard

account.deleteFailedUserNotFound: That account no longer exists. Sign in again and retry.
account.deleteFailedInvalidPassword: That password is not correct. Deletion was not carried out.
account.deleteFailedSystem: The account could not be deleted. Nothing was removed — try again, and contact support if it keeps failing.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.offBody: With two-factor on, signing in also needs a code from your phone — so a password that leaks on its own is not enough to reach your trading book.
twoFactor.scanTitle: Scan this with your authenticator app
twoFactor.scanBody: Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy or any other. Once it is scanned, enter the six-digit code the app shows.
twoFactor.manualKey: Or enter this key by hand:
twoFactor.codesLow: Only {count} recovery codes left. Worth generating a new set.
twoFactor.saveCodesBody: These are what get you in if you lose your phone. They are shown once and never again — put them somewhere safe before you continue. Each one works a single time.
twoFactor.regenerateBody: Generating a new set invalidates every previous code immediately. If you saved them somewhere, they stop working.
twoFactor.disableBody: Turning two-factor off deletes the link to your authenticator app and all recovery codes. From then on your password alone signs you in.
twoFactor.wrongCode: That code is wrong. Check your phone's clock is in sync and try the next one.

manual.daySubtitle: Trades opened and closed on the same day. What you enter here joins the same book as anything that comes from the broker — it will show up in the trades table, on the calendar, in the equity curve and in every breakdown on the analytics screen.
manual.swingSubtitle: Trades held for more than a day. What you enter here joins the same book as anything that comes from the broker — it will show up in the trades table, on the calendar, in the equity curve and in every breakdown on the analytics screen.
manual.moreHint: All optional. Fill in an entry price, a stop loss and a volume and the risk and RR are computed with the same formula the broker sync uses, instead of the amount you typed.
manual.deleteConfirm: Delete this trade? The journal note, the rating and the answers written about it go with it, and there is no broker to re-import it from.
